insights.claim: TrustyAI Explainability Service has no application-level authentication mechanism; all HTTP endpoints are unauthenticated at the application layer.
insights.reasoning: The Quarkus application.properties contains no security extension configuration (no quarkus-oidc, no quarkus-keycloak, no quarkus-security). The OpenShift Route has tls: null, meaning external ingress is plaintext. Authentication enforcement, if any, must be provided by the platform (service mesh, network policies, or an external gateway). This is architecturally significant because the /consumer/kserve/v2 endpoint accepts inference data that could include sensitive model inputs/outputs.

insights.claim: TrustyAI service is tightly coupled to its deployment namespace through the init container's dynamic ConfigMap creation pattern.
insights.reasoning: The init container reads the current namespace from the service account token and creates a model-serving-config ConfigMap with a namespace-scoped URL (http://trustyai-service.$current_namespace/consumer/kserve/v2). This pattern requires TrustyAI to be deployed in the same namespace as the model serving workloads it monitors, and it uses a privileged ose-cli image to run 'oc apply', which requires cluster-scoped ConfigMap RBAC.

insights.claim: RHOAI distribution disables all explainer endpoints while keeping fairness and drift metrics enabled, creating a reduced API surface compared to upstream ODH.
insights.reasoning: The RHOAI Quarkus profile sets endpoints.explainers.local.shap/lime/counterfactual/tssaliency and endpoints.explainers.global to 'disable', while ODH enables all of them. The @EndpointDisabled annotation on endpoint classes enforces this at runtime. This means RHOAI users cannot use local model explainability features (SHAP, LIME, Counterfactual, TSSaliency) or global explanations, which are available in upstream ODH.
